articles.title: Governo Trump aponta plano de espionagem chinês contra CEO da Nvidia, diz jornal | G1
articles.standfirst: Trump teria sido informado sobre as suspeitas há cerca de um ano, mas temia-se que uma reação prejudicasse os negócios da fabricante de chips.
articles.summary: Trump teria sido informado sobre as suspeitas há cerca de um ano, mas temia-se que uma reação prejudicasse os negócios da fabricante de chips.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, durante conferência da empresa em 17 de março de 2026 — Foto: Reuters/Carlos Barria

O governo dos Estados Unidos suspeita que uma executiva chinesa do setor de tecnologia tenha atuado como agente de inteligência de Pequim, enquanto mantinha contato próximo com Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia .

Segundo o The New York Times, Alice Huang, também identificada como Huang Le, era uma das principais executivas da Megaspeed, empresa de data centers sediada em Singapura. Autoridades americanas concluíram que ela repassava informações à China.

A investigação também apura se equipamentos da Nvidia comprados por empresas ligadas à executiva chegaram ilegalmente à China.

Donald Trump teria sido informado sobre as suspeitas há cerca de um ano, mas não tomou medidas. Segundo o jornal, integrantes do governo temiam que uma reação pudesse prejudicar os negócios da Nvidia e complicar as relações entre os dois países.

O caso também envolve a relação entre Huang e Trump. O executivo da Nvidia defendeu mudanças nas regras americanas para permitir a venda de mais chips à China.

No segundo mandato de Trump, o governo autorizou a comercialização de uma geração anterior de processadores em troca de uma participação na receita dessas vendas.

"As interações de Jensen com a sra. Huang não são incomuns nem inesperadas. Reunir-se com clientes faz parte do trabalho de um CEO; Jensen conversa com milhares de executivos de empresas clientes todos os anos", disse John Rizzo, representante da Nvidia, ao jornal.

A Casa Branca, a Agência Central de Inteligência (CIA) e a Agência de Segurança Nacional (NSA) se recusaram a comentar o caso ao jornal.

A Megaspeed informou que sua atual liderança leva o assunto a sério e contratou advogados externos para conduzir uma investigação interna. A empresa também afirmou que pretende cooperar com o governo americano.

Alice Huang não respondeu aos pedidos de comentário. A embaixada chinesa em Washington rejeitou as acusações e classificou a posição americana como infundada.

articles.title: Naufrágio no Amazonas: 16 cilindros de oxigênio são perdidos na seca | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Secretaria de Estado de Saúde, os cilindros perdidos seriam utilizados no atendimento da Unidade Hospitalar Vó Mundoca, em Borba, inclusive em casos de urgência e emergência e no tratamento de pacientes internados.
articles.summary: O naufrágio no Amazonas comprometeu o estoque de oxigênio em Borba, levando o governo a decretar emergência e enviar insumos para 49 cidades em meio à forte estiagem.
articles.body:
O naufrágio de uma embarcação em setembro provocou a perda de 16 cilindros de oxigênio medicinal destinados à Unidade Hospitalar Vó Mundoca , em Borba , no interior do Amazonas. O caso é uma das ocorrências que ajudam a explicar os problemas de abastecimento de materiais de saúde citados pelo governo estadual no decreto que declarou emergência em saúde pública por 180 dias .

Publicado na segunda-feira (26), o decreto considera os impactos da estiagem severa, das queimadas e das dificuldades de transporte no estado . O documento cita acidentes fluviais em Borba, Itamarati e Eirunepé , que provocaram perdas ou comprometeram cargas de medicamentos, insumos e produtos hospitalares.

O acidente envolveu a embarcação Almirante Moreira, que naufragou em 24 de setembro, durante o trajeto entre Manaus e Borba.

Segundo a Secretaria de Estado de Saúde do Amazonas (SES-AM), os 16 cilindros perdidos seriam utilizados no atendimento da Unidade Hospitalar Vó Mundoca, inclusive em casos de urgência e emergência e no tratamento de pacientes internados.

A SES-AM informou ainda que o transporte desses materiais é de responsabilidade das administrações municipais. A pasta afirmou, porém, que presta suporte sempre que solicitada.

Acidentes também causaram perdas em Itamarati e Eirunepé

Em Itamarati, um acidente com embarcação registrado em 21 de agosto de 2026 provocou a perda de medicamentos e materiais destinados à Atenção Primária à Saúde e ao hospital municipal .

Já em Eirunepé, uma carga transportada pela balsa Vovó Amazonas foi exposta à água e à umidade após um acidente nas proximidades de Itamarati. Segundo a gestão municipal, os materiais foram totalmente perdidos .

Governo prevê medidas para manter abastecimento

Para reduzir os riscos de interrupção dos atendimentos, o decreto prevê medidas para manter ou restabelecer o fornecimento de medicamentos, cilindros de oxigênio e outros materiais às unidades de saúde afetadas. O governo também deverá organizar alternativas de transporte e distribuição para as localidades atingidas.

Como parte das ações de assistência, 49 municípios receberam o Kit Calamidade Ampliado, distribuído pela Central de Medicamentos do Amazonas (Cema) .

Os kits reúnem cerca de 106 tipos de itens, que somam aproximadamente 30.027 unidades. Entre os medicamentos estão antimicrobianos, analgésicos, anti-inflamatórios, antiasmáticos, anti-hipertensivos e antidiabéticos, além de soluções e eletrólitos.

A remessa também inclui materiais hospitalares, como luvas, máscaras, aventais, cateteres, seringas, agulhas, gazes, ataduras e fios de sutura.

Estiagem deixou 562 comunidades isoladas

Seca do Rio Negro, na Marina do Davi, em Manaus — Foto: William Duarte/Rede Amazônica

O decreto de emergência em saúde pública terá duração de 180 dias . Segundo o documento, um levantamento preliminar da Defesa Civil estadual identificou 562 comunidades isoladas pela seca dos rios .

A redução dos níveis dos rios dificulta o deslocamento de moradores e o transporte de pacientes, medicamentos e oxigênio medicinal. O cenário aumenta os desafios para manter o atendimento nas localidades mais distantes.

O governo também identificou 19 processos administrativos relacionados a pedidos de medicamentos, insumos, equipamentos, oxigênio medicinal e apoio logístico feitos por municípios.

A SES-AM ficará responsável por coordenar as medidas em conjunto com a Defesa Civil, as prefeituras e outros órgãos estaduais e federais. A secretaria deverá reunir informações sobre as localidades afetadas, as perdas registradas e a capacidade de funcionamento dos serviços de saúde para orientar as ações de resposta.

O Amazonas tem 47 municípios em situação de emergência por causa da estiagem , segundo boletim divulgado pelo governo estadual na noite de quarta-feira (28). Outros 11 municípios estão em alerta e quatro em situação de atenção. Ao todo, 124.221 famílias foram afetadas pela seca dos rios, de acordo com a Defesa Civil.

O levantamento também apontou que Parintins entrou em nível severo (concentrações de MP2,5 superiores a 125 µg/m³ em 24h) por conta da péssima qualidade do ar na manhã desta quinta-feira .

Além disso, foi emitido alerta de nível Alta (concentrações de MP2,5 entre 50 e 125 µg/m³ em 24h) para os municípios de Autazes, Barreirinha, Careiro da Várzea, Iranduba, Itacoatiara, Itapiranga, Manaus, Maués, Nova Olinda do Norte, Novo Aripuanã, São Sebastião do Uatumã, Silves e Urucurituba.

Ações de combate à estiagem e às queimadas

O governo estadual enviou mais de 13 toneladas de alimentos para Anamã e Rio Preto da Eva na terça-feira (27). Os dois municípios receberam, juntos, 670 cestas básicas, 400 kits de limpeza e 200 caixas-d’água de 500 litros.

Com as entregas, a primeira fase da Operação Estiagem 2026 passou a atender 15 municípios. Ao todo, foram distribuídas 4.800 cestas básicas, equivalentes a cerca de 96 toneladas de alimentos, além de 3.400 kits de limpeza e 3.060 caixas-d’água de 500 litros.

A operação também inclui três reservatórios de 5 mil litros e 18 kits purificadores de água. Segundo o governo, as entregas continuarão conforme as condições dos rios e as necessidades das cidades.

articles.title: Acidente na SP-225 em Pederneiras: caminhão de laranjas tomba | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente no km 205 causou interdição total da pista no sentido leste e reflexos no sentido oeste. O motorista teve ferimentos moderados.
articles.summary: Acidente na SP-225 em Pederneiras causa interdição total e lentidão após caminhão de laranjas tombar; motorista foi socorrido com ferimentos moderados.
articles.body:
Um caminhão carregado com laranjas tombou na manhã desta quinta-feira (29) no km 205 da Rodovia Comandante João Ribeiro de Barros (SP-225), no trecho de Pederneiras (SP).

Segundo a concessionária responsável pela administração do trecho, o sentido leste da rodovia precisou ser totalmente interditado, gerando cerca de dois quilômetros de lentidão. Já no sentido oeste, uma das faixas também foi bloqueada devido ao derramamento da carga de frutas sobre a pista.

Caminhão carregado com laranjas tomba e interdita trecho da Rodovia Comandante João Ribeiro de Barros em Pederneiras — Foto: Portal CCM/ARTESP/Divulgação

A pista leste foi liberada por volta das 12h, já a oeste permanecia interditada até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Uma retroescavadeira foi deslocada para o local para auxiliar nos trabalhos de destombamento do veículo e na desobstrução da via. O motorista do caminhão foi socorrido com ferimentos moderados.

As causas e a dinâmica do tombamento serão investigadas.

articles.title: Coreia do Norte lança cerca de 10 mísseis balísticos em direção ao mar na costa leste, afirma Seul | G1
articles.standfirst: Os mísseis de curto alcance foram lançados por volta das 12h30 (horário local) na região de Wonsan, na costa leste da Coreia do Norte, e percorreram cerca de 250 km, informou o Estado-Maior Conjunto (JCS) da Coreia do Sul.
articles.summary: Os mísseis de curto alcance foram lançados por volta das 12h30 (horário local) na região de Wonsan, na costa leste da Coreia do Norte, e percorreram cerca de 250 km, informou o Estado-Maior Conjunto (JCS) da Coreia do Sul.
articles.body:
Soldados do Exército sul-coreano observam o lado da Coreia do Norte, em foto de 16 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: Ahn Young-joon/AP

A Coreia do Norte disparou cerca de 10 mísseis balísticos em direção ao mar ao largo de sua costa leste na quinta-feira, informaram as Forças Armadas da Coreia do Sul, em meio a tensões crescentes antes do prazo estabelecido por Pyongyang para o final do mês, quando os alto-falantes de propaganda serão ativados ao longo da fronteira fortemente armada.

Os mísseis de curto alcance foram lançados por volta das 12h30 (horário local) na região de Wonsan, na costa leste da Coreia do Norte, e percorreram cerca de 250 km, informou o Estado-Maior Conjunto (JCS) da Coreia do Sul.

A Coreia do Sul estava reforçando a vigilância e mantendo-se em prontidão para novos lançamentos, ao mesmo tempo em que compartilhava informações de perto com os Estados Unidos e o Japão, acrescentou.

O Ministério da Defesa do Japão informou que a Coreia do Norte havia lançado o que poderia ser um míssil balístico e que ele não parecia ter caído dentro da Zona Econômica Exclusiva do Japão.

O Gabinete de Segurança Nacional da Presidência da Coreia do Sul convocou uma reunião de emergência para avaliar as implicações de segurança.

O órgão instou a Coreia do Norte a interromper seus repetidos lançamentos de mísseis balísticos, classificando-os como uma “grave violação” das resoluções do Conselho de Segurança da ONU, segundo comunicado presidencial.

“O lançamento pode estar relacionado às tensões ao longo da fronteira como parte de uma série mais ampla de demonstrações de força da Coreia do Norte, embora seja difícil afirmar que a situação na fronteira tenha motivado diretamente o lançamento do míssil”, disse Kim Yong-hyun, professor de Estudos da Coreia do Norte na Universidade Dongguk, em Seul.

Kim afirmou que o lançamento também parecia ter como objetivo demonstrar as capacidades cada vez mais avançadas da Coreia do Norte em mísseis balísticos aos EUA, ao Japão e à comunidade internacional em geral.

O lançamento ocorreu em um momento em que as tensões ao longo da fronteira intercoreana aumentaram drasticamente desde que duas explosões de minas na Zona Desmilitarizada, em 21 de setembro, feriram três soldados sul-coreanos.

Seul afirma que as minas foram plantadas pelas forças norte-coreanas e classificou o incidente como uma violação do armistício, exigindo um pedido de desculpas. Pyongyang negou a responsabilidade e acusou Seul de inventar o incidente.

Kim Yo Jong, a influente irmã do líder norte-coreano Kim Jong Un, anunciou na semana passada que Pyongyang colocaria, em poucos dias, alto-falantes capazes de transmitir propaganda contra a Coreia do Sul em estado de prontidão ao longo da fronteira.

Ela havia dito anteriormente que as transmissões entrariam em operação ao longo de toda a fronteira até o final de outubro, embora analistas em Seul tenham questionado se os aparelhos seriam ativados.

“Em vez de ser uma decisão firme de iniciar as transmissões, a Coreia do Norte parece estar dizendo que terá tudo pronto e observará como a Coreia do Sul reagirá”, disse Lim Eul-chul, professor da Universidade Kyungnam, em Seul.

articles.body:
Filipe Bragança vive o navegador Amyr Klynk numa cena de '100 dias' — Foto: Divulgação

Os filmes "Razão e Sensibilidade" , "Três Horas para Viver" , "As Dez Vantagens de Morrer Depois De Você" , "O Bosque Selvagem" e "100 Dias" estreiam nesta quinta-feira (29) nos cinemas de Boa Vista .

Ao todo, 16 filmes estão em cartaz nos cinemas da capital. Confira a programação abaixo .

Com o brasileiro Rodrigo Santoro, o filme "Três Horas para Viver" acompanha um transportador de elite que recebe uma missão para entregar um órgão para salvar a vida de uma menina de 7 anos. A tarefa vira uma corrida contra o tempo quando uma organização criminosa entra em cena.

Estrelado pelas cantoras Any Gabrielly e Giulia Be, "As Dez Vantagens de Morrer Depois de Você" acompanha Gabriela, que, após a morte da melhor amiga, descobre que ela deixou dez cartas com desafios para ajudá-la a superar o luto.

Adaptada do livro "Cem Dias Entre Céu e Mar", escrito por Amyr Klink, a trama de "100 Dias" é ambientada em 1984 e mostra o navegador decidido a fazer algo que nunca tinha sido feito antes: atravessar o Oceano Atlântico Sul a remo, num barco que ele mesmo projetou.

articles.title: Terenos supera 90% de cobertura de esgotamento sanitário em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Com avanço no município, 36 das 68 cidades atendidas pela PPP entre Ambiental MS Pantanal e Sanesul já apresentam cobertura superior a 90%
articles.summary: Com avanço no município, 36 das 68 cidades atendidas pela PPP entre Ambiental MS Pantanal e Sanesul já apresentam cobertura superior a 90%
articles.body:
Terenos passou a integrar o grupo de municípios de Mato Grosso do Sul que superaram 90% de cobertura de esgotamento sanitário. O avanço, registrado no início do último trimestre de 2026, representa mais uma etapa da expansão dos serviços de coleta e tratamento de esgoto no Estado. Com o resultado, chega a 36 o número de municípios atendidos pela Ambiental MS Pantanal que ultrapassaram essa marca, o equivalente a mais da metade das 68 cidades contempladas pela Parceria Público-Privada (PPP) firmada com a Sanesul em 2021.

O resultado acompanha a ampliação da infraestrutura de saneamento no interior de Mato Grosso do Sul, onde a cobertura de esgotamento sanitário nos municípios atendidos pela PPP alcança 81,2%. Os avanços são resultado de investimentos na implantação e ampliação de redes coletoras, ligações domiciliares, estações elevatórias e sistemas de tratamento de esgoto.

Em Terenos, a infraestrutura operacional conta com uma Estação de Tratamento de Esgoto (ETE) e quatro Estações Elevatórias de Esgoto (EEEs), que integram o sistema responsável pela coleta, pelo afastamento e pelo tratamento dos efluentes gerados no município, cuja população é estimada em mais de 18 mil habitantes.

Para o diretor-executivo da Ambiental MS Pantanal, Clayton Bezerra, o avanço da cobertura de esgotamento sanitário em Terenos reflete os investimentos na ampliação dos serviços e seus benefícios para a população.

“Superar 90% de cobertura de esgotamento sanitário é um marco importante para Terenos. Mais do que ampliar a infraestrutura, estamos contribuindo para a promoção da saúde pública, a proteção dos recursos hídricos e o desenvolvimento local. É um avanço que representa mais qualidade de vida e novas perspectivas para a população”, destaca.

A ampliação da cobertura de esgotamento sanitário em Mato Grosso do Sul contribui para o cumprimento das metas estabelecidas pelo Marco Legal do Saneamento, que prevê o atendimento de 90% da população com coleta e tratamento de esgoto até 2033. Para alcançar esse objetivo, além da expansão da infraestrutura, é necessário garantir a conexão dos imóveis às redes disponíveis e a prestação adequada dos serviços.

Além de Terenos, outros municípios atendidos pela Ambiental MS Pantanal já superaram 90% de cobertura de esgotamento sanitário. Entre eles estão: Alcinópolis, Amambaí, Anaurilândia, Angélica, Antônio João, Aral Moreira, Bataguassu, Batayporã, Bodoquena, Bonito, Brasilândia, Caracol, Chapadão Do Sul, Dois Irmãos Do Buriti, Dourados, Figueirão, Inocência, Itaquiraí, Ivinhema, Japorã, Jateí, Juti, Laguna Carapã, Nova Andradina, Novo Horizonte Do Sul, Paranaíba, Paranhos, Ponta Porã, Porto Murtinho, Ribas Do Rio Pardo, Santa Rita Do Pardo, Selvíria, Sete Quedas, Tacuru e Três Lagoas.

Expansão dos serviços continua na região

O avanço registrado em Terenos também acompanha a expansão da infraestrutura de esgotamento sanitário em outros municípios da região Centro-Norte de Mato Grosso do Sul. A proximidade com Campo Grande, onde a Águas Guariroba já alcançou 95% de cobertura de esgoto, reforça o cenário de ampliação dos serviços na região.

Entre os municípios atendidos pela PPP, Alcinópolis e Figueirão também apresentam cobertura superior a 90%. Já Camapuã, Pedro Gomes, Rio Verde de Mato Grosso, Sonora e Sidrolândia recebem intervenções voltadas à ampliação dos sistemas de esgotamento sanitário.

Em Coxim, as obras realizadas no primeiro semestre de 2026 integram o planejamento de expansão da infraestrutura, com previsão de retomada das intervenções em 2027.

Além dessas localidades, a Ambiental MS Pantanal mantém obras em outros municípios do interior, como Água Clara, Bonito, Caarapó, Eldorado, Fátima do Sul, Itaquiraí, Ivinhema, Maracaju, Naviraí, Ribas do Rio Pardo, Rio Brilhante, Taquarussu, Vicentina, Paranaíba e Itaporã.

A Ambiental MS Pantanal integra a Aegea Saneamento, grupo presente em 892 municípios de 15 estados brasileiros. Atualmente, Mato Grosso do Sul alcança 82% de cobertura de esgotamento sanitário.

No interior do Estado, a Ambiental MS Pantanal atua por meio da Parceria Público-Privada (PPP) firmada com a Sanesul e é responsável pelos serviços de coleta, afastamento e tratamento de esgoto em 68 municípios, onde a cobertura chega a 81,2%.

Em Campo Grande, a Aegea está presente por meio da Águas Guariroba, responsável pelos serviços de abastecimento de água e esgotamento sanitário da Capital, que atualmente alcança 95% de cobertura de esgoto.

articles.summary: Iniciativa da Prefeitura de São Paulo facilita o registro e o pedido de castração de cães e gatos, promove evento de adoção e amplia os horários da vacinação antirrábica
articles.body:
Serviços gratuitos serão oferecidos na Semana Animal SP — Foto: Acervo/SMS

A Prefeitura de São Paulo realizará, de 7 a 14 de novembro, a quinta edição da Semana Animal SP com uma programação voltada à saúde e ao bem-estar de cães e gatos e também às pessoas.

Entre os serviços oferecidos estão: vacinação antirrábica com horários ampliados, identificação por microchip, emissão do Registro Geral do Animal (RGA) e do termo de castração, além de oportunidades de adoção responsável.

As ações são coordenadas pela Secretaria Municipal da Saúde (SMS), por meio da Coordenadoria de Saúde e Proteção ao Animal Doméstico (Cosap) e da Coordenadoria de Vigilância em Saúde (Covisa). Criada em 2022, a iniciativa recebeu quase 100 mil visitantes e realizou mais de 60 mil serviços nas quatro primeiras edições.

Os atendimentos ocorrem em diferentes regiões da capital, facilitando o acesso dos tutores aos serviços. A microchipagem, a emissão do RGA e do termo de castração terão pontos e datas específicos, que podem ser consultados nos links de cada ação.

Já a vacinação antirrábica, obrigatória anualmente para cães e gatos com mais de três meses de idade, estará disponível nos postos fixos participantes, com horários ampliados durante o evento.

A adoção também é destaque na programação. Durante toda a semana, será possível conhecer cães e gatos disponíveis na Cosap, em Santana, para receber um novo lar.

No dia 14, o Especial Gatinhos será dedicado aos felinos, com filhotes e adultos. Os animais são castrados, vacinados, vermifugados, identificados por microchip e registrados com RGA.

Para adotar, é necessário ser maior de idade e apresentar documento de identificação com foto e comprovante de residência emitido nos últimos 90 dias. Quem pretende levar um cão deve ter coleira e guia; para gatos, é necessário caixa de transporte. A taxa pública de adoção é de R$ 35,80.

Nos dias 7 e 8 de novembro, o complexo Cosap/DVZ também receberá atividades educativas e interativas sobre guarda responsável, animais sinantrópicos e prevenção de zoonoses.

A Semana Animal inclui ainda ações de saúde para os tutores e visitantes, como vacinação contra febre amarela e sarampo, caxumba e rubéola (SCR), testagem rápida gratuita para HIV e sífilis e práticas integrativas, como auriculoterapia e Tai Chi Pai Lin.

articles.title: Ex-PM do Piauí foragido por homicídio é preso em Alagoas | G1

articles.summary: Investigado por homicídio e pistolagem, ex-PM do Piauí foragido da Justiça é preso em Taquarana durante operação integrada entre as polícias de AL e PI.
articles.body:
Imagem ilustrativa de pessoa algemado — Foto: Reprodução

Um ex-policial militar do Piauí foragido da Justiça foi preso nesta quarta-feira (28), no município de Taquarana, na região de Arapiraca, em Alagoas. Segundo a Força Integrada de Combate ao Crime Organizado no Piauí (FICCO-PI), ele era procurado por um mandado de prisão preventiva expedido pela Justiça piauiense por suspeita de homicídio qualificado por motivo fútil.

A prisão foi realizada em uma ação conjunta entre a FICCO do Piauí, a FICCO de Alagoas e a Polícia Militar de Alagoas (PMAL). De acordo com a força-tarefa, o suspeito foi localizado após o compartilhamento de informações de inteligência e a realização de diligências integradas nos dois estados.

Conforme a FICCO, o ex-PM também havia sido citado em investigações relacionadas a outros crimes, entre eles pistolagem, roubo, tráfico de drogas e contrabando.

Após a captura, o homem foi encaminhado para os procedimentos legais e permanecerá à disposição da Justiça.

articles.title: Pesquisa do IFMA desenvolve absorvente biodegradável com fibras de sementes de juçara | G1
articles.standfirst: Produto aproveita resíduos de juçara e tem potencial para reduzir impactos ambientais e combater a pobreza menstrual. Pesquisa conquistou o 3º lugar no Prêmio Fapema 2026 e resultou em pedido de patente.
articles.summary: Produto aproveita resíduos de juçara e tem potencial para reduzir impactos ambientais e combater a pobreza menstrual. Pesquisa conquistou o 3º lugar no Prêmio Fapema 2026 e resultou em pedido de patente.
articles.body:
Estudantes do IFMA desenvolveram absorvente biodegradável com fibras de sementes de juçara. — Foto: Divulgação/IFMA

Uma pesquisa do Instituto Federal do Maranhão (IFMA) desenvolveram um absorvente íntimo biodegradável feito com fibras naturais de sementes de juçara, fruto conhecido como açaí em outras regiões do país. A proposta é aproveitar resíduos que costumam ser descartados para criar um produto de higiene menstrual com potencial de baixo custo e menor impacto ambiental.

O projeto foi desenvolvido no Campus do IFMA em São Luís pelas estudantes Sabrina Mendes e Haylana Lima, bolsistas da pesquisa e alunas do curso técnico em Meio Ambiente, sob orientação da professora Laurinda Siqueira, no programa de iniciação científica do Ensino Médio.

O produto tem potencial para contribuir com o enfrentamento à pobreza menstrual e a redução do impacto ambiental causado por absorventes descartáveis convencionais.

De acordo com a pesquisa, as fibras das sementes de juçara passaram por tratamentos alcalino e peróxido-alcalino para modificar sua estrutura e favorecer a absorção.

Em seguida, as pesquisadoras avaliaram a capacidade de absorção, o inchamento, a solubilidade em água, o pH, a desintegração sob agitação e a degradação do material.

Nos testes com uma solução que simula a viscosidade do sangue, o absorvente apresentou índice de absorção equivalente a 3,57 vezes a massa seca do produto. O resultado foi superior aos valores citados na literatura para outras fibras naturais, como algodão (0,84), cânhamo (1,40) e linho (1,57).

Os experimentos também indicaram rápida desintegração sob agitação em água e redução de até 92% da massa em 90 dias, à temperatura ambiente. Segundo os resultados da pesquisa, os dados apontam para o potencial biodegradável do material

Protótipo utiliza fibras de sementes de juçara, resíduo do processamento do fruto. — Foto: Divulgação/IFMA

O estudo vem sendo realizado há cinco anos e foi a primeira experiência científica das duas bolsistas. Atualmente no terceiro ano do Ensino Médio, Sabrina Mendes e Haylana Lima comemoram o prêmio e a participação como coautoras do pedido de patente.

“Para mim isso representa uma conquista muito grande. É evidente que o estudo e a ciência nos levam a lugares que aparentemente estão distantes da nossa realidade”, diz Sabrina Mendes.

As estudantes destacam ainda que o trabalho permitiu desenvolver habilidades laboratoriais, de comunicação e escrita científica, além de ampliar a visão crítica sobre questões ambientais e sociais.

“O que me motivou foi quando começamos os estudos bibliográficos e percebemos o quanto a pobreza menstrual é um problema no Brasil e no mundo. Foi muito gratificante fazer parte de uma pesquisa que busca ajudar tanto as mulheres quanto o meio ambiente”, comenta Haylana Lima.

Produto pode contribuir para combater a pobreza menstrual

O baixo custo do produto pode ajudar a ampliar o acesso à higiene menstrual. A pobreza menstrual é caracterizada pela falta de acesso a absorventes, infraestrutura adequada e informações sobre menstruação e saúde menstrual.

Além do possível impacto social, o aproveitamento das sementes de juçara pode abrir oportunidades para futuras cadeias produtivas locais e valorizar recursos nativos

Sabrina Mendes e Haylana Lima desenvolveram, sob orientação da professora Laurinda Siqueira, um absorvente biodegradável feito com fibras de sementes de juçara. — Foto: Divulgação/IFMA

A professora Laurinda Siqueira afirma que a partir da pesquisa, as estudantes aprendem a formular hipóteses, realizar experimentos, interpretar resultados e reconhecer os limites das próprias conclusões.

“Mais do que isso, percebem que a ciência pode contribuir para responder a necessidades reais da população”, afirma.

A próxima etapa é avançar nos estudos para aprimorar o produto, com novos testes e experimentos. A expectativa é que, futuramente, a tecnologia possa beneficiar a sociedade em maior escala.

A pesquisa conquistou o terceiro lugar do Prêmio Fapema 2026, na categoria Pesquisador Júnior, e também resultou em um pedido de patente no Instituto Nacional da Propriedade Industrial (INPI).

articles.title: MPT processa Meta e pede R$ 50 milhões por assédio eleitoral | G1
articles.standfirst: Ação pede que Instagram, Facebook e Threads removam, em até 24 horas, publicações que incentivem empresários a vigiar, expor ou demitir funcionários por causa do voto. Meta disse que não comenta o caso.
articles.summary: Ação pede que Facebook, Instagram e Threads removam, em até 24 horas, publicações que incentivam empresários a vigiar, expor ou demitir funcionários por causa do voto.
articles.body:
Ministério Público Eleitoral afirma que Meta não cumpriu medidas para tratamento igualitário às campanhas presidenciais — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) entrou nesta quinta-feira (29) com uma ação na Justiça contra a Meta, dona do Instagram, Facebook e Threads.

O órgão pede que a empresa retire do ar, em até 24 horas , publicações que incentivem empresários a vigiar, expor, deixar de contratar ou demitir funcionários por causa do voto.

➡️ O MPT também pede R$ 50 milhões de indenização por danos morais coletivos.

Após o segundo turno das eleições, em 25 de outubro, perfis nas plataformas passaram a publicar mensagens dirigidas a empregadores.

Empresários, influenciadores e até parlamentares orientam patrões a vasculhar as redes sociais de trabalhadores para descobrir em quem eles votaram e, caso a escolha seja diferente da sua, demiti-los.

Outras publicações expõem trabalhadores à ridicularização, com nome e imagem, ou comemoram demissões.

Segundo o MPT, apenas quatro publicações de um único perfil, que tem selo de verificação e 3,8 milhões de seguidores, somavam mais de 2 milhões de curtidas .

Entre a meia-noite de 26 de outubro e as 12h desta quinta-feira (29), o MPT recebeu 1.459 denúncias de assédio eleitoral . Ao todo, foram registradas 3.396 denúncias nas eleições deste ano .

Na ação, o MPT afirma que a Meta tem responsabilidade pela circulação desse conteúdo . Segundo o órgão, além de permitir que publicações consideradas ilegais permanecessem no ar por dias, os sistemas de recomendação da empresa, como a aba “Explorar” e os Reels sugeridos, ampliam o alcance de conteúdos que geram mais engajamento.

As postagens continuavam disponíveis dois dias após a publicação, embora as próprias regras da Meta prevejam a remoção de conteúdos que violem a lei.

Para o MPT, a empresa já dispõe de sistemas automatizados, combinados com revisão humana, capazes de identificar e remover outros tipos de conteúdo em larga escala.

“Se não os emprega para identificar a incitação à discriminação de trabalhadores por convicção política, é por escolha, e não por impossibilidade técnica”, afirmam os procuradores que assinam a ação.

Em caráter de urgência, o MPT pede que a Meta:

Remova, em até 24 horas, publicações de assédio eleitoral, sob multa de R$ 500 mil por conteúdo mantido no ar;

exiba a todos os usuários brasileiros um aviso de que não compactua com manifestações que incentivem discriminação, retaliação ou punição de empregados por orientação política;

notifique os perfis responsáveis por conteúdos ilegais;

suspenda por 30 dias os perfis que voltarem a publicar esse tipo de conteúdo;

desative as contas em caso de nova reincidência.

O órgão também quer que a Meta crie uma política permanente de prevenção ao assédio eleitoral , altere suas regras de uso para proibir expressamente esse tipo de conteúdo, reforce a moderação durante períodos eleitorais e preste contas periodicamente à Justiça .

A ação é assinada pelo procurador-geral do Trabalho, Gláucio Araújo de Oliveira, pela procuradora-chefe do MPT-SP, Vera Lúcia Carlos, e pelos procuradores Igor Gonçalves, Luciana Coutinho, Tatiana Amormino, Diego Jimenez e Marcos Cutrim.

O g1 procurou a Meta, que informou, em nota, que não comentará o assunto.

articles.title: Days after the US Department of Energy announced Power Grid Emergency in 13 States; government declares national emergency to secure bulk power system: What it is, and what it means for Americans
articles.summary: US government has announced a national emergency to protect the country’s electricity grid from potential security risks posed by foreign-made equipment.
articles.body: US government has announced a national emergency to protect the country’s electricity grid from potential security risks posed by foreign-made equipment. In an executive order signed by President Trump, the government authorised restrictions on certain foreign-made equipment that could pose risks to national security, including equipment used in power generation, transmission and grid operations. The order also allows officials to impose security conditions on existing installations and replace equipment deemed risky. The move comes days after the US Department of Energy issued an emergency order in 13 States on October 12 authorising PJM Interconnection, the regional transmission operator serving much of the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions, to run designated power generation units as needed to protect grid stability.What the national emergency means in this caseThe national emergency declaration allows the US government to take stricter measures against foreign-made equipment that could pose security risks to the country's electricity grid. Under the order, the Energy Department can restrict the purchase, import and installation of certain equipment if officials determine that it could expose critical infrastructure to cyberattacks, unauthorised access or supply disruptions.Notably, the order does not ban all foreign-made electrical equipment. Instead, it targets equipment linked to designated foreign entities that the government considers a security risk. It also allows officials to impose security requirements on existing installations, including monitoring, isolation or replacement of equipment deemed unsafe.Why is US doing this nowThe order says the risks have become more serious as the US becomes increasingly dependent on reliable electricity to support AI data centres, advanced manufacturing, defence production and other critical infrastructure.“The rapid growth of advanced manufacturing, data centers, artificial intelligence, and defense production has increased the Nation’s dependence on abundant, reliable electricity and magnified the consequences of a successful attack or supply disruption on the bulk-power system,” the order says.A disruption to the electricity grid could affect businesses, essential services and national security. The administration argues that reducing reliance on potentially vulnerable foreign suppliers would help protect the network.It further stated that the “continued United States reliance on foreign sources of bulk-power system electric equipment with these potential national security vulnerabilities also creates a supply chain vulnerability that could eliminate the supply of these products in the United States as a result of disruptions in international trade or other causes.”What it means for AmericansFor Americans, the national emergency order could lead to tighter security checks on equipment used to supply electricity to homes, businesses and critical infrastructure. The government may require utilities to monitor, secure or replace certain equipment identified as a potential security risk. However, the order does not mean consumers will immediately face changes to their electricity supply.The move could also create opportunities for US manufacturers of transformers, generators and other power grid equipment as the government seeks to prioritise domestically made products. articles.title: Scot arrested in Thailand over alleged phone theft faces six-week verdict wait
articles.summary: Rory McColl was arrested in Bangkok in March over an accusation that he stole a woman's phone - but police say it was a "misunderstanding".
articles.body:
A Scottish backpacker who was arrested in Thailand after he was accused of stealing a mobile phone, faces another six-week wait to find out if he will be allowed to return home.

Rory McColl, 37, claimed he mistakenly picked up a device belonging to a German tourist from a bar in Bangkok thinking it was his own after arriving in the city in March.

The father-of-one, from Edinburgh, spent two nights in a Thai jail, but seven separate court hearings have yet to produce an outcome.

Two police officers testified that the incident was a "misunderstanding" on Thursday, however the case has now been continued for a final verdict on 9 December.

McColl was released on bail following the incident , but had his passport seized meaning he is unable to leave.

His mother, Helen, 70, and dad John, 66, said he had lost his flat and his job as a result of being stranded in the country.

Scots backpacker stuck 'in limbo' in Thailand over mobile phone 'mistake'

Scots backpacker could face jail in Thailand over mobile phone 'mistake'

Helen told BBC Scotland News McColl was "frustrated" following the latest hearing.

"He just wants to see his son," she said.

"It has been so disappointing every time. It is out of our control."

McColl had been enjoying drinks in a bar on the world famous KahoSan Road after arriving in Bangkok following a 30-hour journey.

He claimed to have misplaced his phone before spotting one on the bar.

McColl put the phone in his pocket without realising it belonged to a fellow tourist.

It was returned to the woman a short time later and McColl explained what had happened to the bar's security and the police.

Helen said he had initially been taken to the police station to "sober up" but he was arrested and spent two nights "sleeping on a concrete floor".

After his release on bail, he briefly spent time living in in Pattaya, about 90 miles (150km) south east of Bangkok.

He is now living with a family in the north of country until the case is concluded.

John said his son's mental health had suffered initially, but they were encouraging him to take each day as it comes.

He said: "Rory is very outgoing by nature, very personable. He never sleeps before the court hearings.

"With all the different cases and hearings, we just had to settle and encourage Rory to keep going."

Helen said she had come out of retirement and was looking after dogs to earn additional income for legal fees.

She said she was not completely hopeful the hearing in December will allow him to return home.

"We're trying not to get too excited," she said.

"There's been so many hearings, we don't give ourselves any great expectations that it will even be over on 9 December.

"But if it is, it will be euphoric, the whole family will be here. It will be like a homecoming."

articles.title: A Kannur moment in Alaska could leave Trump out in the cold
articles.summary: TOI Correspondent from Washington: The United States may be heading for a “Kannur moment” in Alaska leading to a potential political and legislative
articles.body: TOI Correspondent from Washington: The United States may be heading for a “Kannur moment” in Alaska leading to a potential political and legislative gridlock in next Tuesday’s midterm elections. Amid allegations that Democrats have sponsored a candidate with the same name as the Republican incumbent in the state’s Senate race to confuse the voters -- a practice all too common in India -- fears are growing that President Trump may use the controversy to question the legitimacy of the entire election process, something he has done often.The name Dan Sullivan has leapt into the headlines after it was reported that Democratic operatives scouted the state for someone with that name who could complicate the electoral prospects of incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan. They eventually found a retired schoolteacher with that name from a small fishing village, who now insists that he is entitled to run, even as President Trump has jumped into the fracas. He has called for the Democratic candidate Mary Peltola to withdraw from the race and face prosecution. Alaska’s Supreme Court ordered the schoolteacher be allowed on the ballot after election officials initially disqualified him.For Indian readers, the controversy would have a familiar ring, most notably stemming from the 2014 Lok Sabha election in Kannur where Congress candidate K. Sudhakaran lost by just 6,566 votes, while two candidates bearing similar names, K. Sudhakaran Sreesai and K. Sudhakaran Kollod, polled more than 7,100 votes. Congress supporters argued that the namesakes had cost their candidate the election. Whether all those votes would otherwise have gone to him is difficult to establish, but the arithmetic illustrates how a seemingly marginal candidacy can matter in a close contest.This is as likely in Alaska, which is among the least populated American states with only around 600,000 voters, but still elects two senators; same as populous states like California, which has 23 million voters. Polls show the Democrat Peltola virtually deadlocked with the Republican incumbent Sullivan, and even couple hundred votes could change the outcome.Clearly anticipating defeat, Trump has already directed the Department of Justice to preemptively contest a potential Republican loss in the race. The department is also demanding a court hold up certification of a possible Democratic win until it's determined whether voters were confused by having two candidates with the same name on the ballot. Separately, responding to a case brought by the civil rights organization NAACP, which advocates for racial justice and rights for Black Americans, the department said agents and employees from the FBI and the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) will not be ‌serving as monitors, amid growing unease about potential federal and MAGA to swing the elections, which are largely a state subject in America.Indeed, the stakes are considerably larger than one seat or one senator’s political survival in one state. articles.title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge
articles.summary: The provider said any change would need support from the community, the regulator and government.
articles.body:
The company which provides energy to households on the Isle of Man said it has no plans to change the charging structure, following announcements in the UK Autumn Budget regarding the removal of standing charges.

On Wednesday, Chancellor John Healy announced the removal of standing charges - fixed daily fees paid regardless of usage - from household gas bills in England, Scotland and Wales, with costs added to the unit rate instead.

Island Energy said any proposed changes would be subject to consultation with the Communications and and Utilities Regulatory Authority (CURA) on the island.

A spokesperson warned removing standing charges may benefit some customers but could see others pay more.

"The cost currently covered by the standing charge would instead be recovered through the unit price of energy," explained an Island Energy spokesperson.

"This means customers who use less energy could save money, while those who use more could see their bills increase."

Islands Energy Group supplies energy to homes and business in Guernsey, Jersey and the Isle of Man.

The gas utility and energy service provider, which serves about 40,000 domestic, commercial, and industrial customers across the three islands, said any change to the charging structure would need to have the clear support of the community, the regulator and government.

Treasury Minister Michael Crowe said his department was reviewing the various measures set out by the chancellor to understand what the implications might be for the island.

"As we look towards the Isle of Man Budget, in February 2027, our priority is to strike the right balance between supporting people and businesses today and maintaining strong, sustainable public finances for the years ahead," he said.

In accordance with the Autumn Statement, the island will extend the reduction in the VAT rate, from 5% to 0% on domestic electricity supplies, until 30 June 2027.

It will also honor the Customs and Excise Agreement with the UK and continue to apply the cut in fuel duty, by 5p per litre, until 30 June 2027.

A reduced duty rate for red diesel, introduced in June until the end of the year, will also be extended to 30 June 2027.

articles.title: Cappadocia: Rock collapse kills two in Turkey's Cappadocia, local media reports
articles.summary: One of the region's famous rock formations, known as "fairy chimneys", reportedly collapsed outside an open-air museum.
articles.body:
At least two people have been killed and five injured after a rock formation collapsed at a tourist site in Turkey's historical region of Cappadocia, local media is reporting.

One of the rock spires, which are known as fairy chimneys, reportedly disintegrated at the popular open-air museum in the central town of Göreme.

Nevşehir provincial Governor Hüseyin Kök said the victims' bodies had been recovered from under the rubble, but the justice minister warned there could be "other potential victims" still trapped.

The cause of Thursday's incident was not immediately known, however local media reported the collapse could have been triggered by heavy rain.

Turkish media reported that the collapse happened near the entrance to the museum - a Unesco World Heritage site - at about 15:15 local time (12:15 GMT).

In a later post on social media, Justice Minister Akın Gürlek said that "according to initial assessments, two individuals have lost their lives in the incident, and five others have been injured".

He added that a search and rescue operation was continuing at the site.

The Cappadocia region attracts tourists from around the world, who want to see the ancient fairy chimneys - tall, cone-shaped rock formations that are created by volcanic activity.

articles.title: Rwandan genocide: Eric Nshimiye convicted in US for lying about role in the killings
articles.summary: Eric Nshimiye was accused of lying to a jury to protect himself and a fellow perpetrator of the genocide.
articles.body:
A Rwandan man has been convicted in the US of lying under oath about his involvement in the 1994 genocide during the trial of a former university classmate.

A federal jury in Boston found Eric Nshimiye, 54, guilty of perjury and obstruction of justice charges stemming from his testimony in the 2019 immigration fraud trial of Jean Leonard Teganya, who was also accused of participating in the atrocities.

Nshimiye fled Rwanda for Kenya in 1994 and was admitted to the US as a refugee the following year.

About 800,000 people, mostly from Rwanda's minority Tutsi community, were killed by ethnic Hutu extremists during the 100-day genocide.

Prosecutors said Nshimiye concealed his involvement in the genocide to secure entry into the country.

Evidence presented at his trial showed that, while a student at the University of Rwanda in Butare, he took part in attacks of the Tutsi people, including by striking them on the head with a club.

He faces up to five years in prison for each of the four perjury counts and a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison for obstruction of justice.

He is due to be sentenced on 26 January 2027.

"For nearly three decades, this defendant concealed his involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide and the heinous acts of violence he committed, including clubbing people to death," US justice department prosecutor Tysen Duva said.

"Then he lied to immigration officials in order to become a US citizen, and he lied to a federal jury to protect himself and a fellow perpetrator of the Rwandan genocide," Duva said.

Nshimiye's lawyer, Kurt Kerns, said in a statement that they were "obviously ⁠disappointed with the verdict" and would pursue "all avenues of relief".

During his opening statement at the trial in October, Kerns argued that the charges were based on "fabricated accusations", saying Nshimiye was not in Butare when the violence began.

He also said Nshimaye was charged only after testifying as a character witness for Teganya, his former university classmate.

Teganya was sentenced to eight years in jail in 2019 for what prosecutors described as "the most serious form of immigration fraud", after lying about his involvement in the genocide.

He was also accused of participating in at least seven murders and five rapes, but denied being involved in the genocide.

articles.title: Hong Kong leader apologizes for deadly fire that tested Beijing’s grip on city
articles.summary: HONG KONG — Hong Kong’s leader made a rare apology Thursday for a residential fire that killed 168 people last year, announcing that a top housing official would resign after an investigation blamed corruption and regulatory failures for the Chinese territory’s worst human-caused disaster in decades.
articles.body: HONG KONG — Hong Kong’s leader made a rare apology Thursday for a residential fire that killed 168 people last year, announcing that a top housing official would resign after an investigation blamed corruption and regulatory failures for the Chinese territory’s worst human-caused disaster in decades. The Nov. 26, 2025, fire at Wang Fuk Court, a high-rise housing estate in the suburban district of Tai Po, swiftly engulfed seven of its eight towers, killing 110 women and 58 men ranging in age from 6 months to 98 years old. Thousands of others were displaced from their homes at the complex, which was undergoing major renovations at the time of the blaze. The tragedy provoked widespread public grief and anger and was widely seen as the first major test for the Hong Kong government since Beijing imposed a sweeping national security law in 2020 in response to pro-democracy protests. Critics say the law, which Hong Kong and Chinese officials say was necessary to restore stability, has been used to stifle dissent in the former British colony. Calls for accountability and transparency after the fire were quickly met with warnings from Hong Kong and Chinese officials, who said that “external hostile forces” were trying to re-create the chaos of the 2019 protests, which sometimes turned violent. John Lee, Hong Kong’s top leader, said he was “deeply saddened” by the fire’s impact on the community. “After self-reflection, I have considered that the government should roll out a large number of measures for reform, and a lot of work has to be carried out,” he said at a news conference. “In my capacity as chief executive, I apologize to all the victims and members of the public,” said Lee, who bowed in apology with seven other senior Hong Kong officials. Lee said Housing Secretary Winnie Ho had resigned on Wednesday, making her the first official to lose her job over the fire. Ho “should bear political responsibility” for the disaster, he said, despite no evidence of personal wrongdoing. Lee also said the government would make changes to Hong Kong’s construction industry and regulatory system based on recommendations from a scathing report by a government-appointed independent committee that was also released Thursday. The fire was the result of “decades of failure by the bodies in positions of responsibility in the construction, fire safety engineering and building management industries, and the Government,” according to the 1,154-page report, which was submitted to the government last week and was partially redacted upon its public release. The long-awaited report found that the fire was most likely caused by a lit cigarette that ignited combustible materials nearby. During public hearings earlier this year, the committee heard testimony that construction workers had been smoking on site. Renovation contractors also used non-fire-retardant scaffolding nets and flammable foam boards to cover windows, which put the “lives of all residents in WF Court at serious risk, apparently with a view to maximizing their financial gains,” the report said. The report said that Prestige Construction & Engineering Co., the main contractor, and project consultant Will Power Architects Co. had “cut corners in numerous aspects.” “There is no doubt that they are the main culprits responsible for the occurrence of the inferno and the high fatalities in the tragic incident,” it said. Both companies, along with seven individuals, were criminally charged in June on 25 counts, including manslaughter, money laundering and tax evasion. The report also took a broader view of Hong Kong’s building maintenance and renovation sector, citing a “corrupt eco-system” long characterized by practices such as bid-rigging, which it recommended be criminalized. In addition, the report criticized the government over regulatory lapses and a “slack enforcement attitude” at the housing complex, where residents had repeatedly raised safety concerns. “The Committee finds that no Government department took effective ownership of various fire safety issues, and complaints about fire hazards fell into a vacuum,” the report said. Lee said Thursday that the Housing Bureau, Buildings Department, Fire Services Department and Labor Department all bore some responsibility for the blaze and that all four agencies would be the subject of a three-month investigation. John Burns, a professor emeritus of politics and public administration at the University of Hong Kong, said it was “very significant” that Lee had apologized. “We’ve gone for years with no chief executive talking about political accountability, as though it didn’t exist,” he told NBC News in an interview. “Today, we have the chief executive talking about this directly and talking about a system of political accountability,” Burns said. “That’s a positive step.” He added that it was “inevitable” that an official such as Ho would resign, “otherwise the credibility of the government itself would have been even more severely damaged.”

articles.title: DHS told '60 Minutes' weeks before segment aired that deported Malian national had once claimed to be gay
articles.summary: Fox News Digital confirmed DHS emailed CBS News weeks before "60 Minutes" aired, revealing Moussa Diawara claimed to be gay on his asylum form.
articles.body: "60 Minutes" was told weeks before the segment aired that a deported Malian husband and father, who was the subject of a sympathetic report on Sunday, claimed to have been gay in his asylum application, Fox News Digital confirmed. Fox News previously obtained records showing Moussa Diawara alleged in his 2009 asylum application that he would face persecution if he were sent back to Mali due to his sexuality. The "60 Minutes" segment depicted an anguished father deported to Africa with his wife and two children still living in the U.S. and noted that a U.S. judge said Diawara could be persecuted, pointing to fears over converting to Christianity. However, the show did not mention that Diawara’s application contradicted his family man narrative and the reason why he claimed he couldn’t return to his native country was because of his sexual orientation. DEPORTED MIGRANT WHO '60 MINUTES' PAINTED AS SYMPATHETIC FAMILY MAN CLAIMED HE WAS GAY ON ASYLUM APPLICATION Fox News Digital has since obtained a copy of an email sent to CBS News by the Department of Homeland Security informing the network about Diawara's claim, which was first reported by The New York Post. The email was sent Oct. 6, nearly three weeks before Sunday's segment aired. A spokesperson for CBS News declined to comment. FROM THE HUNTER BIDEN LAPTOP TO KAMALA HARRIS EDITS: THE LONG HISTORY OF '60 MINUTES' CONTROVERSIES On his 2009 asylum application, Diawara said he feared for his life as a gay man if he was forced to return to Mali. "My asylum application is based upon ground of well-founded past persecution and an undisputable fear of life-threatening [sic] to my person if I were to return to my country Mali. In fact, I had experienced extreme punishment and persecution based on the ground of my sexual orientation," Diawara wrote in his asylum application. "Since I came to the USA I had the possibilities [sic] to express my feelings to men without any embarrassment no reserve. Indeed, my tribal group and community as a whole had reported my sexual orientation to my family back home because such behavior is unwelcome in my society," he continued. "My life is hence worth threatened if I have to go back to my country because I could be executed either by the Islamic group or the community." CBS SHOOTS DOWN 'POLITICAL INTERFERENCE' CLAIMS IN AFTERMATH OF '60 MINUTES' FIRINGS DHS General Counsel James Percival, who was interviewed in the "60 Minutes" segment, took to social media after it aired, saying the newsmagazine made Diawara the "poster child for what it claims are wrongful deportations." "His claimed reason for fearing Mali was that he is ‘gay,’ just in case you’re wondering how bad the immigration fraud problem is," Percival wrote. The segment put a spotlight on Diawara, who was living in the U.S. for 25 years without a criminal record, overstaying his tourist visa and getting nabbed by ICE and sent to Ghana, which ultimately sent him to his home country of Mali. According to the report, Diawara has since fled to an undisclosed African country. During the segment, Percival noted there is "a lot of fraud" in the immigration system and many "fear claims" are untrue. A "60 Minutes" insider previously defended the integrity of the report, pointing to how Diawara's claim that "part of the reason he didn't feel safe" was for religious reasons did make the broadcast. According to the report, he had converted to Christianity, and Mali is a Muslim-majority nation. "The broadcast acknowledged DHS questioned the credibility of Moussa Diawara's fear of persecution, which they're claiming now on social media," the insider told Fox News Digital. articles.title: Labour MP Tony Vaughan apologises over bullying and harassment
articles.summary: Tony Vaughan is found to have been "overbearing and belittling" towards a female staff member.
articles.body:
A Labour MP has said sorry in the House of Commons following complaints over his behaviour towards a female member of staff.

It comes as the Independent Expert Panel published a report requiring Tony Vaughan to apologise for breaching Parliament's bullying and harassment policy.

The MP for Folkestone and Hythe was found by the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards to have committed the breach after a constituency staff member complained he "behaved towards [her] in an overbearing and belittling manner".

Vaughan said on Thursday he accepted the findings in full.

"As a result of these behaviours, my former colleague was upset and humiliated," he said.

"My behaviour had a real and continuing impact on her and her family, and I am truly sorry for this."

The Labour Party said it "expects the highest standards of conduct from all our members and elected representatives.

"We have robust processes in place to ensure those high standards are upheld.

"It is right that Tony Vaughan has apologised following this independent process," a spokesperson added.

Vaughan, who has represented his Kent constituency since 2024, was found to have hugged the complainant without consent at an office event.

He also took her personal mobile phone from her hand to join an online meeting without asking permission and failed to explain why phone calls between them had ended abruptly.

Vaughan appealed the Commissioner's findings, though the Independent Expert Panel confirmed the majority of them, according to Parliament.

The sub-panel stressed that "oppressive and bullying behaviour towards [MPs'] staff members is wholly unacceptable".

It added that Vaughan's actions were breaches of "basic boundaries and courtesy" - rather than failures in management - and an "abuse of his power".

The politician told MPs on Thursday that he was not "sufficiently alert" to the power imbalances between him and his employee.

He added he recognised his behaviour could well impact on "someone who is vulnerable whether or not that is known".

The 36-page report said it took account of the impact of what happened on the complainant, who has a right to anonymity.

She said she was left feeling stressed, exhausted and offended, it adds.

The report also stated that Vaughan had "expressed genuine and thoughtful remorse".

He should be required to make an "unreserved apology" to the complainant and the House by way of a personal statement in the House of Commons Chamber, it continued.

"We consider that this achieves the appropriate balance and clear messaging required regarding the behaviour expected of MPs," the report said.

Vaughan added he had undertaken further training as a result of the incident.

articles.summary: Britain’s king Charles III has acknowledged the suffering caused by slavery amid his nine-day Caribbean tour.
articles.body: Britain’s king Charles III has acknowledged the suffering caused by slavery amid his nine-day Caribbean tour. His "acknowledgement" was addressed to the growing calls for the UK to apologise and pay reparations for its role in the transatlantic slave trade.Speaking at a youth rally in Nassau, the Bahamas, on Tuesday, the 77-year-old monarch "recognised the great suffering and injustices of the past”. He also confirmed thats the legacy of slavery would be discussed by Commonwealth leaders at their upcoming summit.Charles will also visit Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda during the tour. He and Queen Camilla are scheduled to attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), which brings together leaders from 56 nations.Caribbean leaders push for reparationsThe king's visit comes amid renewed demands for Britain to address its historical role in the forced transportation of millions of Africans across the Atlantic into slavery.Commonwealth Secretary-General Shirley Botchwey said last week that the time had come to discuss reparations. Asked by Sky News whether the king should apologise for Britain’s role in the slave trade, she said, “It wouldn’t hurt to have that.”“That’s what the countries have asked for,” Botchwey added. “I don’t believe we can run away from it. But it is important to determine the form that reparations should take, and that is something that will emerge eventually.”The Caribbean Community, known as Caricom, which has 23 member and associate member states, also said last month that it would push for reparations to be discussed at CHOGM.“The Caribbean has consistently asserted that reparations is fundamentally about justice,” Caricom Secretary-General Carla Barnett said. “It is about recognition, accountability and transformation, and about building a just and equitable future for the descendants of those who, as the chattel of colonial owners, endured untold suffering, loss of life and freedom.”UK government rules out formal apologyDespite the pressure, Buckingham Palace has said Charles will not issue an apology during the tour, arguing that such matters are “matters for governments to address”. The palace added that he would “not shy away from the darkest days of our past.”As monarch, Charles represents Britain abroad on the advice of the government. UK Foreign Office sources have told CNN that there is no legal case for reparations because slavery was not illegal when it was practised.At the previous CHOGM in 2024, Charles said “the most painful aspects of our past continue to resonate”, but stopped short of issuing a formal apology.Britain’s Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said on Tuesday that reparations were not a “reasonable request”. He said he was “sensitive to British history” and added that “we should be able to talk about it”, but argued that current generations should not be held responsible for past events.Britain’s slave trade legacyThe monarchy has adopted a more conciliatory tone in recent years. During a visit to Kenya in 2023, Charles said the “wrongdoings of the past are a cause of the greatest sorrow and the deepest regret.”An estimated 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery by European merchants between the 15th and 19th centuries. Britain is believed to have been responsible for transporting about 3.2 million of them.When slavery was abolished in Britain in 1834, the government compensated slave owners an amount equivalent to £17 billion ($22.5 billion), according to research by University College London. Enslaved people received no compensation.On Wednesday, Charles is due to meet the Bahamas’ prime minister and governor general. He will also meet families of four Royal Bahamas Defence Force Marines killed in May 1980 when Cuban MiG fighter aircraft sank HMBS Flamingo following a dispute over illegal fishing. articles.title: Ernie Johnson set to hang up his NBA microphone after this season
articles.summary: Longtime “Inside the NBA” host Ernie Johnson announced Wednesday that this season behind the desk will be his last, ending a career that made him one of the most prominent voices of pro basketball.
articles.body: Longtime “Inside the NBA” host Ernie Johnson announced Wednesday that this season behind the desk will be his last, ending a career that made him one of the most prominent voices of pro basketball. Johnson thanked show staff and co-hosts Shaquille O’Neal, Kenny Smith and Charles Barkley, calling his “Inside the NBA” gig as the ultimate “get-to” position for the past 37 years. “I’ve long described it as a ‘get-to job.’ I’m still amazed that I get to do this for a living,” Johnson said. “It’s been an honor to share so many nights, decades actually, at the desk with my brothers — Kenny, Charles and Shaq — and with our production crews who are so talented and devoted. And I so appreciate the leadership at TNT and ESPN for allowing the show to continue.” At age 70, Johnson said the homework he needs to do for every show had become enough a burden to make 2027 the year to step away. The host has been fighting heart disease for at least two years and underwent bypass surgery 14 months ago. He also was previously diagnosed with non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, a cancer of the lymphatic system, in 2003, and prostate cancer in 2019. “So why now?” Johnson said. “Total honesty here. I’ve always prided myself on my preparation. The hours I put in every day, getting ready for the next show. I’ve always loved that part of my job. But I’ve always vowed that if that ever became more of a challenge than it is a joy, then I’ll know it’s time to step away.” He added: “I know after 37 seasons, it’s time.” Johnson’s stint on “Inside the NBA” began in 1990 on TNT and TBS before the show moved to ESPN last year. Smith joined the show full-time in 1998 before Barkley was added in 2000 and then O’Neal in 2011. Johnson’s retirement also throws in question Barkley’s future as a broadcaster. Barkley has called the two of them “a package deal,” and the 63-year-old former Philadelphia 76er, Phoenix Sun and Houston Rocket appeared to fight back tears as he thanked Johnson for all his work. “That was tough,” Barkley said on ESPN’s “NBA Tip Off.” “We knew the day was coming, still tough. (I’ve) been here for 26, 27 years and it’s been an honor and privilege to work with you all this time.” Barkley said when he meets fans off camera, they always want to know more about his co-workers. “ ‘Where’s Shaq and where’s Kenny,’ like I keep them in my damn back pocket,” Barkley said. “But the question I’m probably asked the most is, ‘Is Ernie Johnson as good a person as he seems?’ And I say, ‘Man, he’s better than that.’ ”

articles.title: This Budget was micro and that was deliberate
articles.summary: Chancellor John Healey's plans fall short of radical action to create a promised new economic model.
articles.body:
It was not a mini Budget, but it was rather small. It might be called the "micro Budget".

Small does not necessarily mean bad, but it clearly falls short of radical action to create a promised new economic model.

A new "theory of growth" was not unveiled as promised by the prime minister Andy Burnham.

It was preamble, roadmap, consultation, perhaps the starter to the main course, which appears to be the PM's 10-year plan next month.

It went unsaid, but the clear stategic aim of Healey's statement was to be the "anti-mini Budget".

This "steady as she goes" predictable fiscal event set out to avoid the aftermath seen following Liz Truss's mini-budget, in which unexpected and unfunded tax cuts spooked the bond and currency markets.

The markets didn't even flicker on Healey's announcement of £65bn of extra borrowing over the next five years - government interest costs have actually fallen since Wednesday, against the backdrop of market turmoil due to the US-Iran war.

The core of the Budget was to get Downing Street through the impacts of the Middle East conflict shock on energy and borrowing costs.

If these pressures prove enduring there are some unpalatable decisions that will have to be grasped within the next year. The can will have to be picked up rather than kicked down the road again.

It buys more time, more "breathing space", as it were, for the government and the prime minister's long-term strategic plans.

The detail may come more quickly than feared. On welfare, the Milburn Review process is clearly heading for some sort of welfare-to-work scheme, even a separate system for younger workers.

It will cost money up front to subsidise work opportunities and hope to save more from welfare bills in the future. The chancellor saw at close quarters Gordon Brown do this twice two decades ago.

The Office for Budget Responsbility's (OBR) economic forecast showed the sheer rise in the welfare bill, which is set to jump to £431bn in 2031, if pensioner support is included.

There are two further areas where the chancellor laid down markers, with little fiscal cost, in terms of the long term plan.

On energy, there is some significance to the "cheaper power" mission announced, reshaping what had previously been a focus on clean power.

While still committed to Net Zero, a series of technical changes to powers over levies and renewable auctions, will seek to turn the tide on additional pressures on energy costs.

On devolution, the plan to allow local mayors to keep some extra business rate and income tax revenues, are more radical than expected.

There are trade offs here, but it essentially provides incentives for regional leaders to grow their economies, workforce and tax base, that are normal elsewhere, but have not existed in the UK's very centralised tax system.

How the PM will square other aspects of his "theory of growth" with the chancellor's spending constraints is the other significant challenge.

Can he announce a 10-year plan without detailing the Liverpool to Manchester high speed train line, or a rebirth of some cancelled HS2 lines he championed a year ago?

Away from the long term, the OBR forecast point to a very tricky economic backdrop until the spring, and a trickier spending review, given the need to accommodate the new defence target of 3% of national income by 2030.

The PM's insistence he will not call an election for a year are eminently believable given the risk of 5% inflation and declining household income.

A "focused" Budget at an uncertain time achieved its narrow aim of a bit of "breathing space" for households and also for the government itself.

But the evident gaps in the Budget will need filling in come the PM's upcoming 10-year plan.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss
articles.summary: The defeated presidential candidate says he will lead the opposition from the US.
articles.body:
The defeated candidate in Brazil's presidential election, Flávio Bolsonaro, has referred to himself as "leader of Brazil" in a letter he published on social media after leaving the country for the United States.

Bolsonaro lost to his left-wing rival, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, in the run-off on Sunday by a difference of 4.4 million votes, but has not conceded defeat.

In the letter, Bolsonaro alleges, without offering evidence, that he was the victim of "electoral fraud" and says that he will lead the opposition from the US.

He left Brazil on Tuesday after failing to comply with an order to surrender his passports, a decision which Lula described as "a shameful act".

Bolsonaro starts his letter, which he posted on his X account, saying "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the leader of Brazil".

However, he had posted a previous version, that was later deleted, in which he wrote: "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the rightful president of Brazil."

Both versions repeat the allegation that Bolsonaro first made on election night, that an extension of polling hours on Sunday had benefited his rival.

In the letter, he says it was "an electoral fraud unfolding before my eyes".

The extension was requested by both Lula's and Bolsonaro's campaign teams, and the head of Brazil's electoral authority has said that the vote proceeded normally and in full accordance with the country's laws and constitution.

An analysis of election data conducted by BBC Brazil and BBC Verify has also found that only around 34,000 people voted during the extended hours - far lower than the 4.4 million votes that separated Lula from Bolsonaro.

In his letter, Bolsonaro also addresses his departure from Brazil - which caused confusion after he disappeared for more than 24 hours .

It later emerged that he had gone across the land border to Argentina, and from there flew on to Florida, following a brief refuelling stop in Ecuador.

Bolsonaro left after failing to hand in his passports to police - in defiance of a Supreme Court order, which had been issued as part of an investigation into alleged money laundering.

He has not been charged as part of the money laundering probe and denies any wrongdoing, calling the investigation a "politically-motivated witch hunt".

Bolsonaro added that he had never intended to leave Brazil, but argued that he was the victim of "political persecution".

He ended the letter by saying: "I left Brazil but I haven't abandoned Brazilians".

While Flávio Bolsonaro said that he planned to lead the opposition from the US, it was not clear how he planned to do that.

His party recognised the election result and while some of its politicians have described Bolsonaro as a "political exile", his campaign manager, Rogério Marinho, stated on Wednesday that "there is no evidence" of the electoral fraud that Bolsonaro alleges took place.

It is also not yet clear where Bolsonaro intends to stay or for how long.

His younger brother, Eduardo, has been in self-imposed exile in the US since March 2025, saying he was the victim of political persecution. The two siblings posted a photo of themselves holding a Brazilian flag on Wednesday.

The Trump administration has provided visas for Flávio Bolsonaro and his family but did not say what kind of visas they were.

The US president did not explicitly endorse Bolsonaro in the run-up to the election and told reporters he "won't get involved" when asked about Bolsonaro's allegations of election fraud.

Earlier in the week, he had said that "it looked like another rigged election," without providing any evidence.

And on Thursday, Trump told reporters that "the election was a very great embarrassment to the people of Brazil".

articles.title: London Zoo animals given pumpkin treats ahead of Halloween
articles.summary: Zoo keepers say they use pumpkins as a way to encourage the animals’ natural instincts and skills.
articles.body:
Animals at ZSL London Zoo in central London enjoyed a Halloween treat today, as pumpkins were hidden around their enclosures containing different types of their favourite foods.

Daniel Simmonds, animal ops manager at London Zoo, said Halloween gives the zookeepers "a great opportunity to come up with new seasonal ways to encourage our animals' natural instincts and skills".

He explained that the keepers lay down scent trails which lead to the pumpkins, and in some cases hide their food inside to encourage foraging.

It is part of an annual tradition at the zoo, and comes as ZSL celebrates its 200th anniversary this year.
